$comment: Accepted occurrences of the backend settled-read-state shapes (see scripts/check-settled-read-states.mjs and docs/adr/0010-settled-read-states.md). Each entry states why this read's collapse of 'failed' into 'empty' cannot be mistaken for an all-clear — or, where it can, says so and names the fix, so the count is pinned honestly rather than hidden. The list may only SHRINK: adding an entry admits new debt and needs the reason to hold up in review; a stale entry fails the gate so a fix must delete its line. Do not add a read whose value is published as a count, a cap, a warning, or a safety fact.

accepted.handlers/plants/handler.ts::resolveActor: Activity-feed attribution. 'Someone' is an explicit unknown, not a claim: a member row with no name renders the same word, and the feed row it labels is advisory — the mutation it describes has already succeeded regardless. Logged as actor_name_lookup_failed.
accepted.handlers/plants/import.ts::resolveActorN: Same helper as handlers/plants/handler.ts, same reasoning: 'Someone' names the unknown rather than asserting anything, and the import rows it labels are advisory. Logged as actor_name_lookup_failed.
accepted.handlers/plants/health.ts::checkPlantHea: Inline form of resolveActorName for the plant.health_checked activity row. 'Someone' is an explicit unknown; the health assessment itself was already returned to the caller before this lookup runs. Logged as actor_name_lookup_failed.
accepted.handlers/tasks/handler.ts::resolveComple: Attribution for a completion record. The email local-part is the documented rendering for an account with no name attribute, and a failed member read renders the same guess. It is persisted as completedByName, so the guess outlives the outage — a cosmetic consequence, not a care-state one; nothing downstream decides anything on it. Logged as completer_name_lookup_failed. A fix would render an explicit unknown on failure; delete this line when it lands.
accepted.services/cognitoUsers.ts::getUserName::c: Display-name lookup. The email local-part is the documented fallback for an account with no name attribute, and a failed Cognito read renders the same fallback. It addresses a person in an email or feed row; nothing acts on it.
accepted.services/climate.ts::readCache::catch-re: A cache. Miss and read failure both correctly mean 'ask the provider': the weather read that follows is the source of truth and carries its own settled states (WeatherLookupResult), and the budget counter it consults fails closed on its own. Nothing is published from this value. Logged as weather.cache_read_failed.
accepted.services/enrichment.ts::readCacheEntry::: A cache. Miss and read failure both correctly mean 'ask Perenual': every caller then passes through upstreamCallPermitted and a discriminated provider result, so nothing is published from this value. Logged as perenual.cache_read_failed.
accepted.services/identifyBudget.ts::incrementUsa: Both null branches mean 'no new total came back'. A successful ADD always returns the attribute, so the `: null` on the success path is a malformed-response guard rather than an empty result, and the documented contract — null means the write may not have counted, callers treat it as soft — holds on either path. Never rendered as 0.
accepted.services/leafHealthBudget.ts::incrementU: Same contract as identifyBudget.incrementUsage: null on either path means 'no new total', a successful ADD always returns one, and callers treat null as soft. Never rendered as 0.
